title: On-call & Incident Response Playbook - Process, Runbooks, Rotations, and Templates
author: Mariana Gomez
content:
Summary
-------
This playbook documents Redwood Inference's standard on-call and incident response processes, runbook index, postmortem policy, rotation schedules, game day guidance, and customer/status-page communication templates. It is intended for on-call engineers, incident commanders (ICs), platform SREs, and engineering managers. Follow the procedures below for production incidents impacting the Redwood hosted API, Dedicated, and Private deployments.

Scope & Ownership
------------------
- Scope: All production-facing services in the Redwood stack: inference-gateway, model-router, kv-cache, batching-service, auth-service, and observability pipeline (metrics/logs/traces).
- Primary owner: Engineering (eng-sre + eng-platform).
- Tiered support: Product/customer-success for customer communications; Security for incidents involving data exposure.
- Tools: PagerDuty (paging & escalation), Slack (#incidents), Statuspage (public status), Confluence (runbooks & postmortems), JIRA (incident tasks).

Incident Severity & SLOs
------------------------
- Sev 1 (P0): Service-wide outage or major degradation causing >50% request failures or >100ms tail latency increase affecting tiered SLAs. Target response (MTTA) = 15m, MTTR < 4h.
- Sev 2 (P1): Partial outage, single-region degradation, or feature-breaking regression for a subset of customers. MTTA = 30m, MTTR < 24h.
- Sev 3 (P2): Degraded performance for a small subset of customers or noncritical functionality. MTTA = 4h, MTTR < 3 business days.

Defined SLOs (examples)
- API availability: 99.95% monthly for hosted endpoint.
- p95 latency for small prompt path: <120ms.
- Embeddings throughput SLOs defined per dedicated pool contract.

Incident Lifecycle (step-by-step)
----------------------------------
1. Detection & Alerting
   - PagerDuty alert or customer report triggers initial page.
   - On-call primary acknowledges within MTTA. If not acknowledged within escalation window (see rotations), PagerDuty escalates to secondary.
2. Triage (first 15 minutes)
   - Identify affected services, regions, models, and scope.
   - Post an initial incident message in #incidents Slack: short summary, Sev level, IC assigned, and initial hypothesis.
3. Assign Roles (within 30 minutes)
   - Incident Commander (IC): owns coordination, customer comms, and timeline.
   - Primary On-call: performs debugging and mitigation steps.
   - Secondary: supports and takes over if needed.
   - Communications lead: posts to status page and drafts customer messages.
4. Mitigation
   - Follow the relevant runbook (see Runbook Index) to apply mitigations: traffic routing changes, autoscaling triggers, model fallback to smaller variants, or rolling restarts.
   - Implement short-term mitigations to restore service (e.g., route to healthy region, enable cached responses).
5. Recovery & Validation
   - Validate through synthetic checks and customer telemetry.
   - Ensure service remains stable for a 30-60 minute observation window depending on severity.
6. Post-incident Cleanup
   - Revert emergency config-only changes when safe.
   - Open follow-up JIRA issues for root cause remediation, testing gaps, and monitoring improvements.
7. Postmortem
   - Author the postmortem (see Postmortem Process). Completed for all Sev1/Sev2 incidents and select Sev3s.

Runbook Index (high-level)
--------------------------
Each runbook page contains: service owner, runbook steps, critical commands, dashboards, rollback steps, and escalation contacts. Key runbooks:
- inference-gateway-runbook: traffic routing, TLS, and connection pooling checks.
- model-router-fallback: model variant fallbacks and KV cache warm-up.
- kv-cache-degradation: eviction and scaling steps, memory profiling.
- batching-service-backpressure: backpressure counters, throttle config, queue drain steps.
- observability-pipeline: restoring metrics/logs/traces, rehydration procedure for missing telemetry.
- auth-service: JWT introspection and token DB failover.

Quick Runbook Example: inference-gateway (abridged)
1. Check console dashboards: API error rate, request latency, 5xx rate by region.
2. Confirm PagerDuty alert details and recent deploys (CI/CD release notes).
3. If error rate spike + recent deploy in the last 30m: rollback to previous image tag via deploy pipeline.
   - kubectl rollout undo deployment/inference-gateway -n prod
4. If high latency due to NLB connection limits: scale gateway pool, increase connection_max, and clear unhealthy targets in cloud console.
5. Enable read-through cache on kv-cache for user-sessions to reduce origin load: toggle feature-flag ff/kv-read-through -> true
6. Notify IC when mitigations complete and validate with smoke tests.

On-call Rotations & Escalation
------------------------------
- Rotation cadence: Primary on-call is a 7-day rotation (Mon 00:00 UTC through Sun 23:59 UTC). Secondary on-call covers the same week as backup.
- Shift handoff: Outgoing primary posts a handoff note in #oncall-handoffs and the rotation calendar with known issues and ongoing tickets.
- Daily status check: Primary posts a morning check-in in #incidents channel by 09:30 local working time.
- Escalation policy (PagerDuty):
  - T0: Page Primary (immediately)
  - T1: After 5m, page Secondary
  - T2: After 15m, page Platform SRE lead
  - T3: After 30m, page Eng Manager on call and begin executive notification for Sev1
- Coverage for holidays: On-call swaps should be recorded in the rotation calendar and require manager approval at least 72 hours in advance.

Roles & Responsibilities
- Primary on-call: Triage, first mitigation, maintain incident log.
- Secondary on-call: Support, take over if primary unavailable, assist with mitigations.
- Incident Commander (IC): Coordinate cross-team resources, own comms and timeline, ensure postmortem.
- Platform SRE: Provide cluster-level fixes, capacity changes, and kernel-level adjustments.
- Customer Success / Support: Draft and approve customer-facing messages, manage escalations for enterprise accounts.

Game Days & Exercises
---------------------
- Frequency: Quarterly game days per major system (inference path, model onboarding, dedicated pools).
- Goals: Validate runbooks, test playbook timings, verify on-call escalation effectiveness, and exercise status page/customer comms.
- Structure: Scheduled injection -> 1-hour live resolution -> blameless retro -> improvement tickets.
- Example scenarios: large model eviction cascade, KV cache corruption, multi-region traffic failover.

Status Page & Customer Communications
------------------------------------
Public status page guidelines:
- Use Statuspage for public incidents. Record: impact summary, affected components, start time, updates cadence (every 30-60 minutes for Sev1), and resolution details.
- Status page message cadence: initial update within 30 minutes of detection, subsequent updates every 30-60 minutes (or when status changes), final resolution with root cause summary within 72 hours for Sev1.

Customer-facing templates (examples)
1) Initial external status (short):
   - Title: Major outage affecting text generation (Hosted API) - investigating
   - Body: We are currently investigating elevated error rates for the Hosted API affecting text generation requests. Our on-call team has been mobilized and we are working to restore service. We will provide an update within 30 minutes.
2) Customer email for impacted enterprise customers (example):
   - Subject: Redwood Inference - Incident affecting generation (start: 2026-01-15 14:03 UTC)
   - Body: Hello <Customer Name>,
     We are investigating an incident that may be impacting your account's text generation requests. Our engineers have identified a high error rate originating from the model routing layer and have applied mitigations to reduce the impact. We will follow up with a timeline for full recovery and a postmortem. For urgent concerns, contact your CSM or reply to this message.

Internal incident update template (Slack)
- [INCIDENT] <Sev> | <Short summary> | IC: @<name> | Primary: @<name> | ETA: <xxm/h>
- Recent actions:
  - <action 1>
  - <action 2>
- Next steps:
  - <owner> -> <action> (ETA)

Postmortem Process
------------------
- When required: All Sev1 and Sev2 incidents must have a postmortem within 7 business days. Sev3 postmortems are optional but encouraged for recurring issues.
- Template sections: summary, timeline (UTC), root cause, contributing factors, mitigations taken, long-term fix, follow-up JIRA tasks with owners, lessons learned, and action items with due dates.
- Blamelessness: The objective is to identify systemic fixes. Avoid attributing fault to individuals.
- Review & sign-off: Postmortems are reviewed by the oncall-manager and a representative from Product and Security (if applicable).

Incident Postmortem Example (summary)
- Title: Sev1 - Model router memory leak causing 25% failure rate (2026-01-15)
- Summary: A memory leak in model-router v3.2 caused increased OOM restarts and request failures. Short-term mitigation: auto-scale additional model-router replicas and restart unhealthy pods. Long-term fix: fix memory leak in v3.3 and add heap-size alerts.

Metrics, Dashboards & Alerting
-----------------------------
- Key metrics: 5xx rate, p50/p95/p99 latencies, request QPS, error-rate by customer tier, KV cache hit ratio, queue length for batching-service.
- Dashboards: Each service must have an owner dashboard and a runbook dashboard linked from the runbook page.
- Alert thresholds: Keep high-fidelity alerts for severe issues; tune for noise reduction. Include alert playbooks linking to runbooks.

Escalation & Communication Checklist (for IC)
- Confirm severity and scope.
- Assign roles and document in Slack.
- Publish initial status page and customer communications if impacted.
- Keep updates regular and factual.
- Create follow-up JIRA tickets and assign owners before declaring incident closed.
- Ensure postmortem is opened and assigned within 48 hours.

Appendix - Contacts & Tools
---------------------------
- PagerDuty: Redwood Production (service id in PagerDuty console)
- Slack channels: #incidents (coord), #oncall-handoffs, #postmortems
- Statuspage: status.redwood.ai
- On-call calendar: Engineering > Oncall rotations (Google Calendar)
- Contact escalation list: eng-sre-leads@redwood.ai, platform-oncall@redwood.ai, security-oncall@redwood.ai

Revision History
----------------
- 2025-11-12: Created by Mariana Gomez (initial draft).
- 2026-01-10: Review updates to escalation windows and game day cadence (reviewers: E. Brooks, N. Shah).
- 2026-02-01: Published with expanded runbook index and status page templates.

Notes & Next Steps
------------------
- Add explicit runbook pages for dedicated-pool-autoscaler and private-deployments failover (owner: eng-private-deployments).
- Schedule next game day for multi-model routing failover (Q2 2026).
